headline: Nvidia Drags Chips Lower as Money Rotates Into Energy and Materials
body_html:
Nvidia pulled the market lower on Wednesday, falling 3.91% as a brief rebound in the chip giant faded and worries about artificial intelligence returned. The S&P 500 slipped 0.29% and the Nasdaq lost 0.65%.

The pressure on Nvidia had several sources. S&P placed the company on CreditWatch over governance concerns, and a settlement of a long-running lawsuit over crypto-mining revenue drew fresh attention. Vice President JD Vance also said he had been assured that chief executive Jensen Huang is not under a Justice Department investigation. The selling spread across the group: Lam Research fell 5.68%, Micron 4.57% and TSMC 2.01%.

Beneath the surface the tape was healthier. 464 stocks rose and 197 fell. Energy led the sectors with an average gain of 2.10%, followed by Materials at 1.84%, Consumer Staples at 1.28% and Industrials at 1.25%. Semiconductors averaged a 0.66% decline and Healthcare slipped 0.17%.

briefs.headline: Cyclical sectors take the lead
briefs.body: Energy averaged a 2.10% gain and Materials 1.84%, the strongest sectors of the session. Industrials rose 1.25% and Consumer Discretionary 1.10%. Investors favored economically sensitive groups while the largest chip names sold off.

briefs.headline: Ambarella suffers the steepest drop
briefs.body: Ambarella fell 19.77%, the worst showing in the universe. Nutanix dropped 15.19% and Urban Outfitters lost 10.33%. The data provided gives no company-specific reason for these declines, so the sharpness of the moves is the main takeaway.

briefs.headline: Smaller names post the biggest gains
briefs.body: Innio rose 8.21% and SolarEdge gained 8.18%, while Semtech climbed 7.48% even as the broader semiconductor group fell. Floor Decor added 7.09% and BlackLine 6.56%. The leaders came from scattered corners of the market.

briefs.headline: Memory and equipment makers sold hard
briefs.body: Micron fell 4.57% and Sandisk lost 5.57%, while equipment makers Lam Research and Lasertec dropped 5.68% and 5.15%. Semiconductors were the weakest sector of the day, with an average decline of 0.66%.

briefs.headline: Growth revision keeps economy in focus
briefs.body: Reuters reported that third-quarter U.S. economic growth was revised sharply higher and that inflation is broadening out. A stronger economy fits with the day's rotation toward industrial and commodity-linked shares, though it also complicates the outlook for rates.

briefs.headline: Holiday shortens the week
briefs.body: U.S. markets are closed Thursday, November 26, for the holiday. Trading resumes Friday, November 27, but it is a half-day, with markets closing at 1:00 p.m. ET. Investors now have a long gap to weigh Nvidia's slide.
